quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow backgrounds. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign tells drivers that a divided highway is coming.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: As speed increases, so does the risk of death. At speeds above 80 mph, you have almost no chance of surviving a crash. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may get impatient and make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: You cannot leave a child under 8 years old alone in a vehicle if it is unsafe.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Never leave a child under 8 years old alone in a vehicle if there is any risk to their health or safety. A person at least 12 years old must always watch the child and be able to see them.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your high beam headlights.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog. High beams reflect back at you and reduce visibility.

questions.question: If an oncoming vehicle is heading straight at you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn, steer right, and speed up.
Honk your horn, steer left, and brake.
Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk your horn, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk your horn, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: First, honk your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they don't move, steer to the right. Don't steer left because the other driver might correct at the last second and you'll still crash. Brake firmly and steadily. Slowing down even a little will reduce the impact.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Drive at your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Let pedestrians go first.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: You may turn right or left at a green light, unless a sign says you cannot. When you turn, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: If two drivers reach a four-way stop sign at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver can go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, let the driver on your right go first if you arrive at the same time. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Before you turn, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Turn the steering wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You can go if the way is clear.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you pass these signs, you are going the wrong way and risk a head-on collision. Carefully turn around.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents other vehicles from distracting you.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between you and other vehicles. This is the only way to have enough time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go through as soon as the train passes.
Go through when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all tracks clearly before moving.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, do not move as soon as a train passes. Wait until you can see down all tracks clearly. Another train may be coming from the other direction.

questions.question: What do orange signs indicate?

options.text: Work zones.
Regulatory rules.
School zones.
Directions and information.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zones.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones on highways. These diamond-shaped signs have black letters or symbols. They warn drivers that people are working on or near the road.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly from your lane.
Stop and back up.
Continue until you reach the next exit or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue until you reach the next exit or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit or another safe place to turn around. Backing up on a freeway shoulder is illegal.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes unclear.
You become less alert.
You calm down and concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your ability to see clearly, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, reduces your recovery from headlight glare, and increases risky behavior. It does not help you calm down or concentrate.

questions.question: An oncoming car is on your left and a bicyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Go between both of them.
Let the car pass, then pass the bicycle.
Pass the bicycle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bicycle.
questions.explanation: When you have two hazards, handle one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, start from which lane?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: What lane width are motorcycles entitled to use?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way with which traffic signal?

options.text: A solid green light.
A flashing yellow light.
A green arrow pointing left.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left.
questions.explanation: A green left arrow means you may turn left safely. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
Getting ahead of bad drivers in traffic.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to avoid accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you identify dangerous situations and take action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid conflicts with aggressive, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.
No passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead. The road splits into two separate one-way roads with a median between them. You must keep to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Two-way traffic.
Lane shifting.
Low clearance.
Added lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: You can only pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street if:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You need all three conditions to pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street: clear visibility ahead, enough space to return to your lane before oncoming traffic arrives, and a vehicle fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: When a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other drivers are doing, even if it goes against the flagger's instructions.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow the regular traffic laws instead of the flagger's directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the flagger's directions.
questions.explanation: Always follow a flagger's directions in construction zones. Slow down when directed and use caution. Ignoring a flagger is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Are safe if they stand on the floor in the back.
Will not get hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand in a vehicle while it is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand in a vehicle while it is moving.
questions.explanation: Children need special car seats designed for their size. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always keep children properly fastened in a seat.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the vehicle catches you.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles pass. Pull over to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: Drive below the speed limit when:

options.text: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
You see a police car.
You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Slow down when roads are wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when any other condition is not ideal. You can get a ticket for speeding even at or below the posted limit if conditions are dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Fire station.
T intersection.
Left turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs prepare you for road conditions ahead. This sign tells you a traffic signal is coming. Be ready to respond to red, yellow, and green lights and cross traffic.

questions.question: What should you do if your gas pedal gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: If your gas pedal sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral immediately and press the brake pedal steadily. Pull off the road safely and turn off the engine.

questions.question: You may park on the freeway shoulder:

options.text: If you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check directions on a map.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: Parking on a freeway shoulder is not allowed except during an emergency.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light requires you to stop before entering the intersection. You must stop at the stop line and before any crosswalk.

questions.question: Drivers do not have to yield to pedestrians who are crossing against the traffic light.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Remember that pedestrians may cross against the light by mistake.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
If the pedestrian uses a hand signal to ask drivers to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if the pedestrian crosses carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street. This is true even if the pedestrian crosses against a red light or is crossing carelessly.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead of you. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often travel slower than the speed limit on hills. Use caution when approaching a large truck from behind. On a hill with limited visibility, it is illegal to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Overcorrect.
Turn your steering wheel into traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
Release the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Steer in the direction the back of the vehicle is sliding.

questions.question: What happens when you take drugs along with alcohol?

options.text: It increases the risk of causing a crash.
It is no more dangerous than consuming alcohol alone.
It lessens the effect of alcohol on your driving.
It has no effect on your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It increases the risk of causing a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can damage your brain function and hurt your driving ability. Mixing drugs with alcohol greatly increases the chance of a crash.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn but you are not in the proper lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and make the turn from your current lane.
Drive to the next intersection and make your turn there.
Safely change lanes then put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next intersection and make your turn there.
questions.explanation: Never make last-minute turns. If you are not in the correct lane to turn, continue to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

questions.question: You are driving in another driver's blind spot. What should you do?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not stay in another driver's blind spot. Move ahead or fall back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: You can use parking lights instead of headlights when driving at night.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive at night using only parking lights. You must use your headlights when it is dark or visibility is low.

questions.question: You should keep your stereo volume low enough to hear traffic sounds.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Set your stereo volume before you start driving. Turn it down if you cannot hear normal traffic sounds over the music.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
A divided highway begins. Slow down to 35 mph.
Merge ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
The road winds ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves right. The number shows the safe speed for the curve. In this case, you should slow down to 35 mph.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people in them.
You can only turn from certain lanes.
Do not enter.
Both lanes must merge smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people in them.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. These lanes are only for buses and cars with the driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: To be ready for anything ahead on the road, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and both sides constantly.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Keep your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and both sides constantly.
questions.explanation: You can handle dangerous situations better if you spot problems early. Look far ahead, but do not just stare at the center of the road. Look at the entire road and both sides to see problems before you reach them.

questions.question: Drivers may text while driving:

options.text: Never.
Anytime.
If they are very skilled drivers.
If they only look away for a moment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You cannot use a cell phone to text while driving. You also cannot use handheld devices to send or read messages. You can only use your phone if you use a hands-free device for voice calls.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait to move.
Honk your horn and pass the bus on the left.
Drive when you think most kids have gotten off the bus.
Pass the bus before the door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait to move.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has its stop arm out, you must stop completely. Do not go until the stop arm is pulled in.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other cars.
Drive at the speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive close behind the car in front.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When heavy rain makes it hard to see, slow down. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If the rain is too heavy to see clearly, pull over and stop until it lets up.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: A no passing zone
A one-way traffic area
The blind spot around a large vehicle
An area for motor vehicles only

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spot around a large vehicle
questions.explanation: "No zones" are large blind spots around trucks and big vehicles. Drivers in smaller cars should not stay in these "No zones."

questions.question: Alcohol is the number one cause of deaths in car crashes.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Alcohol is the leading cause of death on American roads. It hurts your vision and slows how fast you react. It takes longer to respond in an emergency. Alcohol affects driving even if you are not legally drunk.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: Go.
Let other cars go first.
Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming soon. If you see a yellow light ahead, slow down and prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, go through carefully.

questions.question: Headlights must be on when people or vehicles cannot be seen clearly from 1,000 feet away.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: You must use headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise. You must also use them anytime people or vehicles cannot be seen clearly from 1,000 feet away.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Side road.
Two-way left turn.
Farm machinery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs tell drivers to stop and let other cars go first at an intersection. You can go when it is safe.
